To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
metrics should be published in various forms and channels and that they should be used to engage people in the analysis of the data and the discussion about their meaning.

1) the way in which metrics are presented to people is a key factor in their acceptance, 2) metrics should be used as a tool to tell a story and 3) the story is more powerful if it is told by a trusted source.
metrics and feedback are essential for a healthy agile organization, that dashboards are a necessary but not sufficient means to achieve this and that additional engagement channels can help.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How can we use metrics and feedback to engage people and improve the agile development process?
how to best leverage metrics in the context of agile software development.
the design of metrics and feedback channels that can help teams to improve their processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
metrics are a powerful means to support the continuous improvement process in agile teams but only if they are properly presented and contextualized.
metrics and feedback should not be limited to dashboards.

metrics and feedback should be used to improve the quality of software development and to support the agile principles, but that they should also be used to improve people’s awareness about the process and the product, to improve their understanding of their work, to improve their engagement, and to improve their sense of ownership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more we are able to tell stories about the collected data, the easier it is to engage with the data and to use it to improve the team's performance.
metrics are a powerful tool to support continuous improvement, but only if they are used properly.
the more we can make the data accessible and understandable to people, the more they will use it to support their work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of metrics is not a black and white problem.
the way in which metrics are presented can have a significant impact on the perception of metrics and their acceptance by the team.
there is no one-size-fits-all solution for the use of metrics and that the choice of metrics and of the channels to publish them is a key element of a successful continuous improvement process.
